pujas.title: Shri Radha Krishna Yugal Sarkar Puja
pujas.subtitle: For love, harmony & a blessed married life

about.q: What is the Yugal Sarkar Puja?
about.a: Yugal Sarkar means the divine couple — Shri Radha and Shri Krishna worshipped together. The puja asks for the selfless love of Radha–Krishna to bless your own relationships.
Barsana is Shri Radha's own village. Devotees believe that a prayer offered through Radha Rani reaches Shri Krishna immediately.

about.q: Why in the month of Kartik?
about.a: Kartik is called Damodar Maas and is the dearest month to Radha–Krishna. Lamps and worship offered in Kartik are said to give manifold merit.

about.a: In Vedic astrology, Kaal Sarp Dosh is said to form when all seven planets sit between Rahu and Ketu in the birth chart. It is associated with repeated delays, sudden setbacks and unrest.
Trimbakeshwar is traditionally regarded as the foremost place for Kaal Sarp shanti, performed at the source of the Godavari by hereditary pandits.
It helps but is not required. If you have it, share your date, time and place of birth while booking and our astrologer will note the dosh type.

temples.name: Shri Banke Bihari Mandir
temples.short: Home of Thakur Banke Bihari ji, the 'bent in three places' form of Shri Krishna, in the lanes of Vrindavan.
history: The deity was revealed by Swami Haridas, the saint-musician of Nidhivan, whose devotion is said to have made Radha and Krishna appear as one form.
Darshan here is given in short glimpses — a curtain is drawn every few moments, as devotees believe no one can bear Bihari ji's gaze for long.
The temple is famous for its Phool Bangla in summer, when the sanctum is decorated entirely with fresh flowers.

temples.name: Shri Radha Rani (Ladli Ji) Mandir
temples.short: Hilltop temple of Shri Radha in her childhood village of Barsana, on the Bhanugarh hill.
history: Barsana is revered as the birthplace and childhood home of Shri Radha, daughter of Vrishabhanu Maharaj.
The temple is reached by over 200 steps and looks out over the whole of Braj.
Barsana's Lathmar Holi and Radhashtami celebrations draw devotees from across the world.

temples.name: Sri Mayapur Chandrodaya Mandir
temples.short: The grand temple of Sri Sri Radha Madhav on the banks of the Ganga at Mayapur, birthplace of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu.
history: Mayapur in Nadia district is revered as the appearance place of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, who spread the chanting of the Hare Krishna maha-mantra.
The Chandrodaya Mandir houses the deities of Sri Sri Radha Madhav and the Ashta Sakhis.
Its kirtans, Ganga aarti and festival celebrations make it one of Bengal's busiest pilgrimage centres.

temples.name: Kalighat Kali Mandir
temples.short: One of the 51 Shakti Peethas, beside the old course of the Adi Ganga in south Kolkata.
history: Kalighat is counted among the Shakti Peethas, where the toes of Devi Sati's right foot are believed to have fallen.
The Devi here has a striking form with three large eyes and a long golden tongue, worshipped as Dakshina Kali.
The city of Kolkata is said to take its name from this ancient seat of Maa Kali.

temples.name: Shri Trimbakeshwar Jyotirlinga
temples.short: Jyotirlinga at the source of the Godavari, famed for Kaal Sarp, Narayan Nagbali and graha shanti rituals.
history: The linga at Trimbakeshwar has three faces representing Brahma, Vishnu and Mahesh.
The Brahmagiri hills above the temple are the source of the Godavari, called the Ganga of the south.
Trimbakeshwar's pandits are known across India for dosh nivaran pujas performed by traditional vidhi.

temples.name: Shri Siddhivinayak Ganapati Mandir
temples.short: Mumbai's beloved Ganapati temple, home of the right-trunked Siddhivinayak who grants wishes.
history: The original temple was consecrated in 1801 and has grown into one of the most visited temples in Maharashtra.
The idol's trunk turns to the right, a form known as Siddhi Vinayak, considered quick to bless sincere prayers.
Tuesdays and Sankashti Chaturthi see devotees queue through the night for darshan.

temples.name: Shri Shanidev Mandir, Shingnapur
temples.short: Open-air shrine of Shani Dev — a self-manifested black stone worshipped without a roof.
history: Shani Dev here is a swayambhu black stone standing on an open platform, with no roof or walls around it.
The village is famous for its houses without doors, a sign of the people's faith that Shani Dev protects them.
Devotees offer mustard oil abhishek to the stone, especially on Saturdays and Shani Amavasya.

temples.name: Shri Salasar Balaji Dham
temples.short: Rajasthan's famous Hanuman dham, where Balaji appears with a beard and moustache.
history: The idol is said to have emerged from a farmer's field in 1754 and was brought to Salasar on a bullock cart.
Unusually, Hanuman ji here has a round face with beard and moustache, worshipped as Salasar Balaji.
Devotees tie coconuts with red cloth in the temple compound as a sign of their wish.

temples.name: Shri Gnana Saraswati Mandir
temples.short: One of India's rare Saraswati temples, on the banks of the Godavari, famous for Akshara Abhyasam.
history: Tradition holds that Maharishi Vyasa meditated here and shaped the idol of the Devi from handfuls of sand.
Parents bring young children for Akshara Abhyasam, the ceremony of writing the first letters.
Students visit before examinations to seek the blessing of Maa Gnana Saraswati.

site.name: Radhika Astro
site.description: Book pujas at sacred temples of India in your name and gotra, receive the puja video on WhatsApp and get the Aashirwad Box at your doorstep. Shop authentic gemstones, malas and puja essentials.

globalFaqs.q: How does Radhika Astro perform a puja in my name?
globalFaqs.a: Our partner pandits at each temple read out your name, gotra and wish during the sankalp, then perform the full vidhi. You receive the recorded video on WhatsApp.

globalFaqs.q: My gotra is unknown. Can I still book?
globalFaqs.a: Yes. When the gotra is not known, the shastras allow the sankalp to be taken in Kashyap gotra. Just select “Gotra not known” on the booking form.

globalFaqs.q: Do I need my kundli for graha shanti pujas?
globalFaqs.a: It is helpful but optional. Share your birth date, time and place and our astrologer will check the relevant dosh before the puja.

globalFaqs.q: When will I get the video?
globalFaqs.a: Usually within 2–4 days of the puja date. Night pujas such as Kali Puja may take a day longer.

globalFaqs.q: What comes in the Aashirwad Box?
globalFaqs.a: Prasad, a raksha sutra, kumkum or sindoor from the temple, and a blessed photo of the deity. It is shipped within 8–10 days.

globalFaqs.q: Can I book for relatives in another city or country?
globalFaqs.a: Yes. Add their names in a Couple, Parivar or Sanyukt Parivar package. The video is shared with your WhatsApp number.

globalFaqs.q: What if a puja cannot be performed?
globalFaqs.a: If we cannot perform a booked puja for any reason, the full amount is refunded to your original payment method.

globalFaqs.q: How do I reach the seva team?
globalFaqs.a: Message us on WhatsApp or call the seva helpline from 8 AM to 9 PM IST, all days.
